plan.title: A first interval run, proof that says nothing about it: what they did and noticed gets as much attention as how it felt

context.text: Morning, Dev! First intervals today: 1 min jog, 2 min walk, 4 rounds around the park at 7. A quick voice note when you're done.

transcript.text: [voice: Done, all four rounds.]
Dev, first jog rounds done, 3 step days in a row 🔥 How did the jogging minutes feel compared to the walking?
harder than I expected, rounds 3 and 4 were rough
Rough in rounds 3 and 4 is normal when jogging is new, Dev, and you finished all four anyway 💪 What did rough feel like: breathing, legs, or your head telling you to stop?
idk, I kind of just pushed through them

Pushing through when it gets rough is the skill that gets you to that mile, Dev. That's a real win 💪 Wednesday at 7, want to run the same four rounds again, jogging a touch slower so rounds 3 and 4 feel easier?
oh I think I started the first jog way too fast actually

That's a sharp catch, Dev. Starting slow so rounds 3 and 4 feel easier is the whole trick. So Wednesday at 7: same four rounds of 1 min jog, 2 min walk, with the first jog easy enough that you could still talk. Work for you?
sounds good
Locked in, Dev. Wednesday at 7, easy first jog, voice note after. Go enjoy the rest of your Monday 💪
